query: where are old host log files deleted once they get too old or the folder gets too big
notes: Apply first deletes host-*.log files older than the max age, then deletes the oldest ones until the total size is under the cap.

query: where are the host process command-line arguments like the pipe name and parent pid parsed
notes: Parse reads --pipe, --parent-pid, --token-handle, --log-dir and --version and picks the HostMode.

query: where does the settings service refuse to read or write secret keys
notes: RejectSecretKey throws PolicyDenied for any key under 'secrets.' and is called from both GetAsync and SetAsync.

query: where are file and line references pulled out of build logs and .NET stack traces so they can be cited
notes: SignalCitations matches the MSBuild diagnostic and stack-frame regexes and turns each file:line into a de-duplicated Citation.

query: where is the dollar cost of a saved chat reply worked out
notes: CostOf returns 0 for a local model and otherwise uses the catalog's per-million-token prices with the Outbound record's token counts.

query: which class runs the indexing CPU work on dedicated below-normal priority threads
notes: PipelineScheduler is a TaskScheduler with fixed background threads at ThreadPriority.BelowNormal, so chat and autocomplete always get CPU first.

query: which class shuts the host down when the Visual Studio process that launched it goes away
notes: ParentProcessWatcher waits on and polls the --parent-pid process, then calls HostShutdown.RequestStop when it exits.

query: Which component saves outbound request log records to the local database in the background so requests are never slowed down?
notes: StoreOutboundSink queues each OutboundRecord in a bounded channel, and a single background writer saves them to the conversation store.

query: which service tells the extension when the machine goes online, offline or local-only
notes: ConnectivityHostedService runs the ConnectivityMonitor and sends the connectivityChanged notification after each handshake and on every state change.

query: which class finds index databases on disk and opens them read-only for search
notes: ReadOnlyIndexCatalog finds index folders by their state.json, opens each encrypted database with ReadOnly=true and warms its vector cache.

query: MemoryGovernor halving the embedding batch size
notes: MemoryGovernor lives in PauseGate.cs; BeforeBatch frees memory, then halves the batch, then pauses indexing when the working set is over the cap.

query: HandshakeValidator order of checks
notes: Validate checks, in order, the pipe client pid, the launch token, the request's client pid and contract version compatibility.

query: how does TailTruncation.KeepTail fit text into a token budget
notes: KeepTail keeps the last lines that fit, puts a line-count marker in front, and shrinks the target size each round until the counted tokens fit.

query: HostStateMachine allowed state transitions
notes: IsAllowed looks the move up in the AllowedTransitions table; TryTransition applies it, logs it and raises StateChanged.

query: DiagnosticsRpcService autocomplete latency p50 p95
notes: Build takes recent autocomplete Outbound records and computes first-token and total p50/p95 times with the nearest-rank Percentile helper.

query: how does background indexing back off when the laptop is in battery saver mode
notes: ApplyPower sets the Battery pause reason when the pauseOnBattery setting is on and Win32PowerStatus says battery saver is active.

query: how are RPC calls refused until the client has completed the handshake
notes: DispatchRequestAsync answers any method other than HandshakeAsync with the HandshakeRequired error until the handshake is accepted.

query: when Visual Studio can't answer a find-callers query, how does the host fall back to the index
notes: CallersOfAsync asks Roslyn only when WhyNotRoslyn returns null; any refusal, error or miss goes to FromIndexAsync, which uses the symbol-graph edges.

query: How are passwords and API keys kept out of git diffs and commit logs that get pinned into a chat?
notes: AddPatch hides changes to files the secret-file policy refuses and runs every patch through Redact, which uses LogRedactor to replace secrets.

query: how does the host avoid flooding the extension with a notification for every single settings save
notes: OnChanged restarts a debounce timer; OnTimer then compares snapshots with ChangedSections and sends one settingsChanged with the changed section names.

query: where does the Gemini adapter tell the API whether it is embedding a search query or a document passage
notes: TaskTypeOf maps the embedding purpose to RETRIEVAL_QUERY or RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT, and BuildRequest puts it into the taskType field.

query: where is the automatic profile picked depending on whether we're online or offline
notes: ChooseProfile resolves the Auto profile for each task class: Balanced, Frontier or Fast when a cloud provider is reachable, and LocalStrong or LocalFast when not.

query: where does the Azure provider decide between sending an api-key header and getting an Entra ID bearer token
notes: The constructor builds the request authorizer (api-key first, else a bearer token from ITokenCredentialProvider), and ReadAuthentication parses the auto, apiKey or entra setting.

query: where do model file downloads refuse redirects that leave https
notes: This method follows redirects by hand, caps the number of hops and throws if the next Location is not https.

query: Where are failed HTTP responses from cloud LLM providers turned into user-facing errors like bad API key, rate limited, or prompt too long?
notes: Map sorts statuses and body text into credential, billing, missing-model, context-overflow, 429 and 5xx ProviderExceptions; IsContextOverflow matches the providers' context-length wording.

query: which class decides if a file looks like a secret or is excluded and needs approval before going into a prompt
notes: FileAccessPolicy.Check applies the indexing.exclude globs and the built-in secret rules (.env, .pem, .ssh, appsettings with passwords) and returns a verdict.

query: which component stops sending requests to a provider after it keeps failing
notes: CircuitBreakerRegistry keeps one breaker per provider: it opens after consecutive failures, refuses requests while open, and lets one trial through when half-open.

query: which class works out the context size and keep-alive for local Ollama models so a small GPU doesn't end up running two copies of the same model
notes: OllamaResidency reads /api/ps and returns a ResidencyPlan (num_ctx, keep_alive, CPU-only), unloading and reloading the model when the tier cannot hold a second instance.

query: which class keeps the audit log of every request sent to a model provider
notes: InMemoryOutboundLog stores OutboundRecords (counts only, no prompt text) in a ring buffer, passes each one to sinks and logs a structured line.

query: CompletionShaper stop sequences and the line limit on streamed autocomplete
notes: Push cuts the stream at the first stop sequence or at maxLines, and HeldBack holds back a tail that could be the start of a stop sequence.

query: StreamingPlaceholderRestorer redacted placeholder split across chunks
notes: HoldIndex finds an unfinished <redacted:...> at the end of the buffer so Push waits for the closing > before restoring the secret.

query: EstimatingCounter safety margin token estimate
notes: EstimatingCounter.Count turns characters per token and tokens per digit into a count, adds the safety margin and rounds up, for families without an exact tokenizer.

query: how does WholeScopeParser.Parse handle code fences and echoed line numbers in the model reply
notes: Parse removes a surrounding Markdown fence, keeps the prose as the explanation, and calls EditText.StripLineNumbers to drop the 'N| ' prefixes.

query: how are retries handled when a provider returns 429 or a server error
notes: StartAsync retries before the first token when IsRetryable (429 or 5xx) holds, waiting for an exponential backoff with jitter from Backoff.

query: how is the context window budget divided between project rules, pinned files, the current file and the user's message in a chat prompt
notes: AssembleAsync takes the output reserve and the system prompt off the window and places items in priority order with per-item caps; Place truncates or drops an item to fit min(cap, remaining).

query: how are embedding vectors normalized and compressed before they go into the index
notes: Process scales the vector to unit length and then calls Quantize, which applies symmetric int8 quantisation with one scale per vector.

query: if I keep typing the same characters an autocomplete suggestion already predicted, how is the rest of it served without a new request?
notes: Lookup tries the exact key first, then shorter prefixes (up to 64 typed characters) whose cached completion starts with what was typed, and returns the remainder as a type-through hit.

query: how does applying the model's find-and-replace edits cope with whitespace or indentation that doesn't exactly match the file
notes: FindAtLevels tries exact, then trailing-whitespace, then indentation-insensitive matches; Find retries without blank edge lines; Reindent moves the replacement to the code's indentation.

query: what value of k does ReciprocalRankFusion use by default
notes: DefaultK = 60 is the fusion constant, and RetrievalOptions.RrfK (also 60) is the setting the hybrid retriever passes to Fuse.

query: when a function is too big for one chunk and gets cut into pieces, how is each piece labelled?
notes: Fit packs an oversized unit into parts and labels each with WithPart, which appends " (part n of m)" to the breadcrumb.

query: how are files and symbols ranked by importance for the repo map
notes: Rank builds weighted symbol and file reference graphs, runs PageRank by power iteration in Compute, and boosts by cross-file referrers.

query: which class turns the top-ranked symbols into a compact indented outline that fits a token budget
notes: RepoMapRenderer renders the repo map: focus files first, then ranked symbols, each with its enclosing definitions, within MaxTokens.

query: where are stop words removed and file names picked out of a search query
notes: Analyze tokenizes the query, detects file names by extension or separator, drops stop words, and builds the identifiers, terms and lexical query.

query: how does a retrieval hit get widened to the rest of its split member plus a neighbouring chunk on each side without blowing the token budget
notes: Expand first adds sibling parts with the same breadcrumb segments and part count, then one neighbour on each side, as long as the total stays under maxTokens.

query: which chunker is used for text files that have no language-aware chunker
notes: WindowChunker is the fallback (60-line windows overlapping by 10 lines); FileChunker.Chunk sends unknown or failing languages to it.

query: IdentifierSplitter split rules for acronyms like HTTPServer and digits
notes: Split breaks identifiers on underscores, case changes, the last capital of an acronym, and letter/digit boundaries, then lower-cases the parts.

query: where is the database encryption key created, protected for the current Windows user, and saved next to the database?
notes: Create generates a random key, protects it with DPAPI using Pillion entropy, and writes it with a user-only ACL plus an atomic move; LoadOrCreate decides whether to load or create.

query: where is cosine distance computed for quantized int8 embedding vectors
notes: DotAndNorm computes exact SIMD integer sums, and CosineDistance turns them into 1 - dot/(|a||b|) in the same form sqlite-vec uses.

query: which vector search backend reads every embedding from the table on each search instead of caching them in memory
notes: TableScanVectorIndex scans chunk_embeddings, computes cosine distance in managed code and keeps the top k in a heap, holding no copy of the vectors.

query: why are very common words dropped from the full-text match expression
notes: WithoutCommonTerms keeps only terms found in fewer than half the chunks (or the rarest one) before the FTS5 bm25 query in SearchLexicalAsync.

query: where does file discovery decide from a file's first bytes that it is binary or auto-generated
notes: Inspect looks for a NUL byte in the first 8 KB (UTF-16 BOM files excepted) and for auto-generated markers in the first 2 KB.

query: which class decides which process owns an index and takes over a lock left behind by a dead process
notes: WriterLock runs the writer.lock election with create-new semantics and reclaims stale locks (dead or reused PID) behind a guard file.

query: when does an index get deleted automatically
notes: Decide keeps in-use indexes and deletes ones whose root is gone or that are unused past retentionDays; SweepAsync applies those decisions.

query: FileHasher.Hash xxHash64 fingerprint and modified time
notes: Hash streams the file through a pooled 64 KB buffer into XxHash64, reading the modified time from the handle before the first byte.

query: where are provider API keys saved in Windows Credential Manager
notes: Both write a generic credential with target PillionProgrammer/<name> and a UTF-16 blob: the host-side store and the VS-extension-side store.

query: what values does SecretAllowList treat as placeholders rather than real secrets, e.g. AKIAXXXXXXXX
notes: IsAllowed checks well-known values, placeholder words and shapes; IsFiller flags values made of one repeated character or 60% or more one character.

query: how are redaction placeholders numbered when a single request contains several different secrets of the same kind
notes: Redact registers new distinct values per kind, then uses <redacted:kind> for a lone value or <redacted:kind#n> once there are several.

query: which class figures out how much dedicated video memory the GPU has to pick a hardware tier
notes: GpuTierDetector tries nvidia-smi, then DXGI, then the registry; the largest adapter decides the tier and the result is cached.

query: where are links in chat replies checked before they can be opened in the browser
notes: TryGetSafeUri accepts only absolute http, https and mailto URLs and rejects javascript:, file:, UNC and other unsafe forms.

query: RestartPolicy backoff delays and when it gives up restarting the host
notes: RecordCrash applies 1 s / 5 s / 30 s backoff for consecutive crashes and stops after 3 crashes within a 5-minute sliding window.
